Which experiments matter most for a Moon.answer:
No experiment flew on the Moon, so investigations are matched by oxygen levels and pressure. The ACME-BRE record lists atmospheres NASA considered for human missions, such as 26.5% oxygen at 10.2 psia (about 70 kPa) and 34% oxygen at 8.2 psia (about 57 kPa) [ACME-BRE].

FLEX covers oxygen levels from 12% to 34% and pressures from 70.2 to 309.3 kPa [FLEX]. FLEX-2 covers oxygen levels from 17% to 30% and pressures from 50.7 to 304 kPa [FLEX-2]. ACME-CFI-G covers oxygen levels from 12% to 85% and pressures from 49.5 to 331 kPa [ACME-CFI-G]. ACME-FLAME-DESIGN covers oxygen levels from 19.8% to 85% and pressures from 43 to 306.9 kPa [ACME-FLAME-DESIGN]. For both, the 85% is the burner flow in an inverse flame, not the cabin air [ACME-CFI-G][ACME-FLAME-DESIGN]. In addition, ACME-BRE tested oxygen levels from 21% to 40% [ACME-BRE]. ACME-S-FLAME tested oxygen levels from 21% to 30% [ACME-S-FLAME].

What has NASA tested on detecting smoke.answer: NASA tested smoke detection with overheated spacecraft materials such as Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, lampwick and dibutyl phthalate, using two smoke detectors, thermophoretic smoke samplers and video cameras [SAME]. NASA also tested detection with Kapton, silicone, lampwick, Teflon and Pyrell fire retardant foam, employing an ionization smoke detector, DustTrak and an M-pass instrument [SAME-R]. NASA further tested aerosol detection using Arizona Road Dust mixed with nitrogen, using a modified TSI P-Trak particle counter and DustTrak instrument [DAFT]. The same aerosol detection test was repeated in a second record [DAFT-2].

Which experiments tested putting out fir.answer:
BASS tested putting out solid fuel fires using an inert gaseous extinguishing agent [BASS]. BASS-II investigated extinction limits of solid fuels by lowering the ambient oxygen level below 21% through nitrogen dilution [BASS-II]. 

FLEX tested extinguishing liquid fuel droplets using gaseous suppressants, specifically carbon dioxide and helium [FLEX]. ACME-BRE evaluated flame extinction in still air without forced flow, where flames went out on their own at 21% oxygen [ACME-BRE].
